transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, well, I guess I came in because... I've been having a little bit of a communication hiccup at work. It's probably nothing major, I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right. People keep telling me they can’t really follow what I’m trying to explain lately. Like, when I'm writing my artist statements, or doing client notes, or even just what I say in meetings... I guess I start jumping around a bit? I'll go from talking about textures to the budgets, and then into... well, these secret meanings behind the work. 

I think I'm just being really passionate and creative, but I don't want to confuse my clients or make a bad impression. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Aside from feeling passionate, have you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or invincible lately, to the point where you might not even need much sleep?

Well, um... I guess you could say I've had some stretches where I just feel really, really lit up. Like, almost unstoppable? It's actually a wonderful feeling, honestly. It's like every idea I have for a project is just brilliant and everything clicks. I do stay up a bit later working on things when I feel like that, but I just thought I was being productive. Is that okay? I mean, I hope that's a normal part of the creative process. 

But, um... I suppose there is another side to it. Sometimes, when I'm feeling that energetic, if a collaborator or a client makes even just a small comment or a tiny critique... I can get a little defensive. Or, well, I might snap at them. It's embarrassing to admit, because I really try to be professional and kind to everyone. It just feels like my reaction is a lot bigger than the situation warrants. I'm really trying to work on that, though. I don't want you to think I'm a difficult person to work with.
Have you ever felt that you were receiving special messages or that you had secret knowledge that others around you weren't aware of, even when you weren't feeling that 'lit up' or energetic?

Um... well... I guess I have, yeah. I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, because I know how it might sound, but... there was a quieter month recently. I was actually sleeping pretty normally, and I didn't have that huge, unstoppable energy at all. I thought I was just having a really grounded period. 

But, um... even then, for a few weeks, I kept hearing these... little comments? Like they were coming from right behind the storage shelves in the studio. And I started reading these sort of hidden warnings into just ordinary studio materials, like the way the canvases or tools were leaning against the wall. 

I know that probably sounds really strange... I really hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or anything. I just figured maybe my brain is a little hyper-observant because of my art, and I was just looking too deeply into things. Is that something that happens to people sometimes? I hope it's okay that I shared that.

During that quieter month when you were hearing those comments and noticing those hidden warnings, were you experiencing any of those periods of high energy or decreased need for sleep at the same time?

Um, no... no, I really wasn't. I know I touched on it just a second ago, but I was definitely sleeping my normal hours then. I always try really hard to make sure I get enough rest so I can be reliable for my clients, you know? 

So, no, I didn't have any of that big, unstoppable energy at all during those weeks. I was just feeling very... regular. Calm, I guess. That's why those little comments and the warnings were so confusing to me, because my energy was completely fine. They definitely weren't happening at the same time. 

I... I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means it's just a small quirk and nothing too serious, right? I really am trying my best to manage everything properly.
During those times when you weren't feeling that 'lit up' energy, did you ever experience weeks where you felt deeply sad, hopeless, or completely uninterested in things you usually enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely have days where I feel a little uninspired or maybe just tired, but... I wouldn't say I've had weeks of feeling deeply sad or hopeless. I love my art, and I usually always want to be in the studio, even if I'm just organizing things. 

I think everybody gets a little down sometimes, right? But I always try to push through it and stay positive. I really don't want to be one of those artists who just completely shuts down. I try to keep a good attitude. So... no, I haven't really had anything like what you're describing. I hope that's helpful?
Could you tell me how long those weeks of hearing comments and seeing hidden warnings lasted in total?

Um... well, it's... it's been a little while, actually. I guess if I really think about it, the... the comments and noticing the warnings in the materials, and sometimes even, like, certain smells in the studio... it's been happening for... maybe around eleven months? 

I know that sounds like a really long time, but it's not like it's every single second of the day! It's just... off and on, you know? And I've been able to keep working and everything, so I really didn't think it was that big of a deal. I didn't want to make a fuss over something that might just be, like, an overactive imagination. 

I hope it's okay that I didn't bring it up sooner. I just... I didn't want you to think I was doing a bad job of handling things. Is eleven months a really bad thing? I'm still doing okay, right?
